examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule
examples.problem: Given that $y= 3\cdot 2^{1 - x},$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y = 3\cdot 2^u, \qquad u=1-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = 3\cdot 2^u\ln(2),\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} =-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =3\cdot {2}^{u}ln⁡(2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =-3\cdot {2}^{u}ln⁡(2) \\  & =-3\cdot {2}^{1-x}ln⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=4{x}^{3}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=12{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (12{x}^{2}) \\  & =12{x}^{2}{e}^{u} \\  & =12{x}^{2}{e}^{4{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(12{x}^{2}{e}^{4{x}^{3}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =12(1)^{2}{e}^{4(1)^{3}} \\  & =12{e}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$
